turns.customer: Ridge 2 vs Summit 3 for backpacking, which one should I get?
turns.reply:
Both are 3-season, waterproof (3000 mm), and on the 20% tent sale. Here's how they line up:

| | Ridge 2 | Summit 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Type | 2-person backpacking (freestanding) | 3-person trekking (steep-walled, for long trips) |
| Weight | 1,900 g | 2,600 g |
| Material | 20D ripstop nylon | 30D ripstop nylon (durable) |
| Doors/Vestibules | 2 doors, 2 vestibules | — |
| Rating | 4.6 | 4.5 |
| Price today | $199.20 (was $249.00) | $263.20 (was $329.00) |
| Stock | In stock (green; orange sold out) | Low stock (green; grey sold out) |

My take: for backpacking, grab the Ridge 2. It's the one actually built for backpacking — 700 g lighter for carrying, the same waterproofing, a slightly higher rating, and $64 cheaper. The Summit 3's extra room and tougher 30D fabric come at a real weight penalty, so it suits solo/lone travelers who want headroom on longer, gear-heavy trips rather than weight-conscious hikers.

If you're camping alone but want that extra space and don't mind the 2,600 g, the Summit 3 is the pick. Otherwise, the Ridge 2 wins on weight, price, and rating. Both are only in green right now.

Want me to check stock details or quote a cart total for either one?
